newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight drops to 6.5 pct on intervention.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight drops to 6.5 pct on intervention.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate dropped to 6.5 percent after hitting a high of 8.5 percent earlier as big Malaysian banks stepped in to lend, dealers said on Monday.
They said the banks, which are also agents of Bank Negara Malaysia, came in immediately after the overnight hit 8.5 percent and brought down the offer rate.
"It seems like a central bank operation, but we cannot be sure," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said both borrowers and lenders at the lower level were the big banks, which indicated the possibility of intervention.
A dealer with another Malaysian bank said the central bank probably stepped in to help dispel stock market fears of a tight money market.
Earlier, most interbank rates ended higher due to fears of another U.S. interest rate hike and further tightening of the domestic money market.
One-week money ended at 7.40/50 percent against 7.15/25 on Friday, two-week at 7.35/40 percent against 7.20/30 and three-week at 7.30/35 percent against 7.25/30.
One-month money was at 7.35 percent against 7.30/33, three-month at 7.35/40 against 7.30/35 and six-month at 7.40/45 against 7.35/38.

The dealers said inflation data released in the United States on Friday suggested a strong possibility of a follow up to the 25-basis point hike in U.S. lending rates last month, which could trigger a similar trend in Malaysia.
Dealers were divided over the possible trend in the domestic money market. But they agreed that if there was a flow of funds out of Malaysia, interest rates could be pushed up.
More immediately, on Wednesday, two issues of Bank Negara bills totalling one billion ringgit against a maturity of 500 million was expected to tighten the market further.
Last week, Bank Negara intervened to slow the ringgit's fall by selling nearly $200 million, dealers said. A 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue also reduced liquidity in the flush market.
In line with this trend, interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange (MME) closed lower.
Spot month June contract based on the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) fell one point to 92.69 by 0430 GMT, or an implied yield of 7.31 percent.
September was down one point to 92.68, or 7.32 percent and December eased two points to 92.63, or 7.37 percent.
March 2998 contract fell three points to 92.53, June five points to 92.50 and September four points to 92.50.
